2) Any contractual preference for routing (e.g., do you require onshore-only for certain countries, or is the UK addendum + SCCs sufficient for UK-origin data?).

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers: 
- I attached the APAC subprocessors export (apac-subprocessors.csv) — short list: 3 local caching providers (singapore-cache.example, tokyo-edge.example, sydney-proxy.example) and one analytics partner in India. The caches persist short-lived KV cache entries for 24–72 hours. Analytics keeps aggregated telemetry only.
- For routing: we prefer UK-origin patient records to remain subject to UK Addendum protections. For other APAC countries, we're flexible with SCCs provided the cache TTLs are short and we have contractual limits on downstream analytics.

We also flagged a question: does Redwood require a separate signed TIA for the onshore cache nodes, or can the DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum + an internal operational attestation be sufficient?

Naomi —

Thanks — reviewed the CSV. Quick readout:
- Singapore and Tokyo caches are managed edge providers with ephemeral KV retention (TTL <= 72h) and no persistent PII stores. Under our usual risk model, those can be governed by SCCs + operational attestation (traceability, retention policy, access control logs).
- Sydney-proxy.example retains session tokens for routing (longer TTL) — that one is a borderline processor; recommend a narrow TIA (scope: routing tokens and session metadata) focused on access controls and logging.
- Analytics partner in India processes aggregated telemetry only; acceptable under SCCs but add a contractual clause prohibiting re-identification and a periodic audit right.

Controls I recommend we require before onboarding the pilot:
1) Signed SCCs + UK Addendum for any UK-origin patient data (DocuSign link)
2) Onshore-cache exception: a one-page TIA for Sydney-proxy.example limited to routing tokens with specific controls (encryption-at-rest, RBAC, 90-day access log retention)
3) HSM/KMS: if TideCare wants provider-managed encryption keys for UK-origin datasets, we must confirm KMS integration (note: this affects latency and deployment topology).

I attached a quick mapping (see apac-subprocessors.csv row notes). Happy to draft the one-page TIA template if you want.

—Jonas

All —

Thanks Jonas, that aligns with my read. A couple of commercial/contract asks before we send to TideCare: 
- If we require a one-page TIA for Sydney-proxy.example, we should include a clause limiting liability for transient caches and clarifying retention TTLs.
- Ask procurement to push for the customer to accept our standard UK Addendum redlines; if they insist on alternate language we may need legal to run a redline and that will add 2–3 business days.
- On the KMS point: we can support customer-managed keys via our dedicated deployment model, but if TideCare expects the hosted (shared) keys there’s an SLA/price delta. We should outline that in the next call.

Next steps: Naomi — if you want, I’ll draft the TIA one-pager and a short note to TideCare that summarizes the SCCs + UK Addendum baseline plus the single TIA exception for Sydney-proxy.example. Marissa, please prep the procurement note for pricing delta if TideCare requests customer-managed keys.
